memory_verse.label: Bible Reference
memory_verse.text: "Weave the tunic of fine linen and make the turban of fine linen. The sash is to be the work of an embroiderer. Make tunics, sashes and caps for Aaron's sons to give them dignity and honor. After you put these clothes on your brother Aaron and his sons, anoint and ordain them. Consecrate them so they may serve me as priests." - Exodus 28:39-41 (NIV)

devotion.label: Devotion
devotion.text:
Aaron's sons receive garments too — tunics, sashes, and caps, given for the same reason as their father's: dignity and honour. And notice the order in which they are made priests. First they are clothed, then anointed, then ordained. God dresses them before He commissions them.

That order is significant. They did not earn the garments by serving well; they were given the garments in order to serve. The clothing came first, as a gift, and the ministry followed. Everything they did as priests flowed out of what they had already been given.

The Christian life follows the same pattern. We are not clothed with Christ's righteousness because we served faithfully; we serve because we have been clothed. Paul says that all who were baptised into Christ have clothed themselves with Christ (Gal 3:27), and urges us to clothe ourselves with compassion, kindness, humility, gentleness and patience (Col 3:12). Identity precedes activity. Before God asks anything of you, He has already dressed you in what you need. Serve today out of what you have received, not to earn it.

reflection.label: Reflection
reflection.text:
Am I serving to earn God's approval, or out of what He has already given me?
What has God clothed me with that I have been forgetting to live in?

prayer.label: Prayer
prayer.text: Father, You clothed me in Christ before ever asking anything of me. Help me serve out of what I have received rather than striving to earn what is already mine. Amen.
